Addressing a sea of supporters in São Bernardo do Campo, the industrial city where his political career began nearly half a century ago, the 80-year-old politician reminded voters of the chaos and violence that unfolded during the 2018-2022 presidency of his far-right predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro, whose son, Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula will face in October’s presidential election. President, 80, vows to keep far-right from power as Flávio Bolsonaro tells supporters he will ‘fight this system’ Brazil’s leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has launched his campaign for a historic fourth term and vowed that as long as he lived he would not allow the “shameless” right to return to power. Addressing a sea of supporters in São Bernardo do Campo, the industrial city where his political career began nearly half a century ago, the 80-year-old politician reminded voters of the chaos and violence that unfolded during the 2018-2022 presidency of his far-right predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro, whose son, Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula will face in October’s presidential election.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, 80, said Sunday he was "in great shape" as he launched his candidacy for October elections, with pressure from US President Donald Trump's administration looming over the campaign. A titan of the Latin American left, Lula is seeking a fourth and final term in office in a campaign casting him as a safe pair of hands in turbulent times and a bulwark against the global rise of the far right. While no one mentioned Trump by name at the Workers' Party (PT) convention in Sao Paulo, Lula and fellow leftist heavyweights leaned heavily on the theme of protecting Brazil's sovereignty from outside threats, amid trade and diplomatic spats with Washington. "I want to be prepared so that no one invades this country," Lula said, urging greater investment in defense.

"I want to fight against old age. I don't want to be shuffling along," he said. Brazil's constitution allows presidents to serve two consecutive terms. After a break, they can run again, with no lifetime limit on the number of terms. "The world is in turmoil. Today, we face wars and the rise of the far right. In times of rough seas like these, you need a reliable, experienced sailor," said former finance minister Fernando Haddad, who is running for governor of Sao Paulo state. Lula said he would not run again after a fourth term, as he and his wife Rosangela, 59, would be "going on vacation to focus on romance for another 20 years." The octogenarian's main election rival is Flavio Bolsonaro, eldest son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro.

President, 80, vows to keep far-right from power as Flávio Bolsonaro tells supporters he will ‘fight this system’

Brazil’s leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has launched his campaign for a historic fourth term and vowed that as long as he lived he would not allow the “shameless” right to return to power.

Addressing a sea of supporters in São Bernardo do Campo, the industrial city where his political career began nearly half a century ago, the 80-year-old politician reminded voters of the chaos and violence that unfolded during the 2018-2022 presidency of his far-right predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro, whose son, Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula will face in October’s presidential election.

Lula recalled how hundreds of thousands of citizens died during a Covid outbreak Jair Bolsonaro was accused of bungling with his anti-science policies. Gun ownership soared as laws were relaxed, allowing criminal groups to expand their arsenals. “They handed out … more than a million weapons,” Lula said, promising to dedicate a fourth term to improving education and healthcare as well as developing Brazil’s rare earth deposits, the world’s second largest after China’s.

Lula also said he would improve security by targeting the rich organised crime bosses who lived in luxury apartments. “It’s easy to kill a crook in a favela. But the guy running the show lives in a penthouse … and we need to stop this,” Lula said. He also told his far-right rivals to “show some shame”.

Lula was speaking at the Vila Euclides football stadium, where his astonishing rise to the presidency began in 1979 when, as 33-year-old union leader, he spearheaded two historic strikes that helped end the military dictatorship. Those strikes made Lula a household name and in 2002, after three failed attempts, he won a landslide victory to become his country’s first working-class president.

During Lula’s first two-terms, from 2002 until 2010, he was credited with fighting hunger, dramatically expanding social welfare programmes and access to higher education and improving Brazil’s global standing, although his administration was blighted by corruption scandals. His successor, Dilma Rousseff, became Brazil’s first female president but led the country into a severe economic recession before being controversially impeached in 2016.

The former metalworker and union leader made a dramatic comeback when he returned to power three years ago after a stint in jail on corruption convictions that were later annulled, having previously governed from 2003-2010.

He is loved and despised in near-equal measure in Brazil and won his last election by a razor-thin margin.

payload.title: Lula tavoittelee neljättä kautta – Flávio Bolsonaro haastaa hänet lokakuun vaaleissa
payload.summary: Brasilian 80-vuotias presidentti Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva hakee neljättä ja viimeiseksi lupaamaansa kautta äärioikeiston torjumista ja maan suvereniteettia korostavalla kampanjalla.
payload.content:
Brasilian presidentti Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, käynnisti sunnuntaina kampanjansa lokakuun presidentinvaaleihin ja tavoittelee historiallista neljättä kauttaan, jonka hän sanoo jäävän viimeisekseen. Vasemmistolaisen Lulan tärkeimmäksi vastaehdokkaaksi on nousemassa äärioikeistolaisen entisen presidentin Jair Bolsonaron vanhin poika Flávio Bolsonaro.

Lula puhui kannattajajoukolle São Bernardo do Campossa, teollisuuskaupungissa, jossa hänen poliittinen uransa alkoi lähes puoli vuosisataa sitten. Hän kertoi olevansa hyvässä kunnossa ja lupasi estää äärioikeiston paluun valtaan niin kauan kuin elää. Puheessaan hän muistutti myös Jair Bolsonaron presidenttikaudesta vuosina 2018–2022, jota hän kuvasi kaaoksen ja väkivallan ajaksi.

## Kokemus kampanjan perusteluna

Lula rakentaa kampanjaansa kokeneen ja vakaan johtajan roolin varaan aikana, jota hänen tukijansa kuvaavat levottomaksi. Brasilian perustuslaki sallii presidentille kaksi peräkkäistä kautta. Tauon jälkeen sama henkilö voi pyrkiä virkaan uudelleen, eikä kausien kokonaismäärälle ole elinikäistä rajaa.

Myös ehdokkaan ikä nousi esille kampanjan käynnistyessä. Lula sanoi haluavansa taistella vanhuutta vastaan eikä tyytyä kulkemaan voimiensa hiipuessa. Hän vakuutti olevansa valmis vaalikamppailuun mutta ilmoitti samalla, ettei asettuisi enää ehdolle mahdollisen neljännen kautensa jälkeen.

Lula puhui myös tulevaisuudestaan politiikan jälkeen. Hän sanoi vitsaillen lähtevänsä vaimonsa Rosângelan kanssa lomalle ja keskittyvänsä seuraavat 20 vuotta heidän suhteeseensa.

## Suvereniteetti nousi kampanjan teemaksi

Työväenpuolueen puoluekokouksessa Lula ja muut vasemmiston näkyvät nimet painottivat Brasilian suvereniteetin suojaamista ulkoisilta uhkilta. Yhdysvaltain presidenttiä Donald Trumpia ei mainittu nimeltä, mutta taustalla ovat Washingtonin kanssa syntyneet kauppa- ja diplomaattiset kiistat sekä Trumpin hallinnon aiheuttama paine. Lula vaati suurempia puolustusinvestointeja ja perusteli niitä tarpeella estää tunkeutuminen maahan.

São Paulon osavaltion kuvernööriksi pyrkivä entinen valtiovarainministeri Fernando Haddad vertasi maailman tilannetta myrskyävään mereen ja Lulaa luotettavaan, kokeneeseen merimieheen. Haddadin mukaan sotien ja äärioikeiston nousun leimaama aika korostaa kokemuksen tarvetta.

Flávio Bolsonaro on puolestaan kertonut kannattajilleen aikovansa ”taistella tätä järjestelmää vastaan”. Lokakuun vaaleissa Lula hakee neljättä kauttaan kampanjalla, jonka keskeinen tavoite on estää Jair Bolsonaron edustaman poliittisen leirin paluu valtaan.

Kampanjassa korostuvat äärioikeiston torjuminen, poliittinen kokemus ja Brasilian suvereniteetti.
Lulan tärkeimmäksi vastaehdokkaaksi on nousemassa Jair Bolsonaron vanhin poika Flávio Bolsonaro.

President, 80, vows to keep far-right from power as Flávio Bolsonaro tells supporters he will ‘fight this system’

Brazil’s leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has launched his campaign for a historic fourth term and vowed that as long as he lived he would not allow the “shameless” right to return to power.

Addressing a sea of supporters in São Bernardo do Campo, the industrial city where his political career began nearly half a century ago, the 80-year-old politician reminded voters of the chaos and violence that unfolded during the 2018-2022 presidency of his far-right predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro, whose son, Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula will face in October’s presidential election.

Lula recalled how hundreds of thousands of citizens died during a Covid outbreak Jair Bolsonaro was accused of bungling with his anti-science policies. Gun ownership soared as laws were relaxed, allowing criminal groups to expand their arsenals. “They handed out … more than a million weapons,” Lula said, promising to dedicate a fourth term to improving education and healthcare as well as developing Brazil’s rare earth deposits, the world’s second largest after China’s.

Lula also said he would improve security by targeting the rich organised crime bosses who lived in luxury apartments. “It’s easy to kill a crook in a favela. But the guy running the show lives in a penthouse … and we need to stop this,” Lula said. He also told his far-right rivals to “show some shame”.

Lula was speaking at the Vila Euclides football stadium, where his astonishing rise to the presidency began in 1979 when, as 33-year-old union leader, he spearheaded two historic strikes that helped end the military dictatorship. Those strikes made Lula a household name and in 2002, after three failed attempts, he won a landslide victory to become his country’s first working-class president.

During Lula’s first two-terms, from 2002 until 2010, he was credited with fighting hunger, dramatically expanding social welfare programmes and access to higher education and improving Brazil’s global standing, although his administration was blighted by corruption scandals. His successor, Dilma Rousseff, became Brazil’s first female president but led the country into a severe economic recession before being controversially impeached in 2016.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, 80, said Sunday he was "in great shape" as he launched his candidacy for October elections, with pressure from US President Donald Trump's administration looming over the campaign.

A titan of the Latin American left, Lula is seeking a fourth and final term in office in a campaign casting him as a safe pair of hands in turbulent times and a bulwark against the global rise of the far right.

While no one mentioned Trump by name at the Workers' Party (PT) convention in Sao Paulo, Lula and fellow leftist heavyweights leaned heavily on the theme of protecting Brazil's sovereignty from outside threats, amid trade and diplomatic spats with Washington.

"I want to be prepared so that no one invades this country," Lula said, urging greater investment in defense.

The former metalworker and union leader made a dramatic comeback when he returned to power three years ago after a stint in jail on corruption convictions that were later annulled, having previously governed from 2003-2010.

He is loved and despised in near-equal measure in Brazil and won his last election by a razor-thin margin.

Supporters point to social programs that have lifted millions out of poverty while critics -- noting that the PT has been in power for around 17 of the past 24 years -- highlight enduring problems such as crime and corruption.

"I'm here today because Lula's policies changed my life and my family's. Thanks to him, we own our own home today," Cristiane Rosa Julho, a 51-year-old social worker, told AFP.

Lula argued in his address that his stamina and exercise regime keep him "in great shape."

"I want to fight against old age. I don't want to be shuffling along," he said.

Brazil's constitution allows presidents to serve two consecutive terms. After a break, they can run again, with no lifetime limit on the number of terms.

"The world is in turmoil. Today, we face wars and the rise of the far right. In times of rough seas like these, you need a reliable, experienced sailor," said former finance minister Fernando Haddad, who is running for governor of Sao Paulo state.

Lula said he would not run again after a fourth term, as he and his wife Rosangela, 59, would be "going on vacation to focus on romance for another 20 years."

The octogenarian's main election rival is Flavio Bolsonaro, eldest son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro.

article.summary: Brasilian 80-vuotias presidentti Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva hakee neljättä ja viimeiseksi lupaamaansa kautta äärioikeiston torjumista ja maan suvereniteettia korostavalla kampanjalla.
article.content:
Brasilian presidentti Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, käynnisti sunnuntaina kampanjansa lokakuun presidentinvaaleihin ja tavoittelee historiallista neljättä kauttaan, jonka hän sanoo jäävän viimeisekseen. Vasemmistolaisen Lulan tärkeimmäksi vastaehdokkaaksi on nousemassa äärioikeistolaisen entisen presidentin Jair Bolsonaron vanhin poika Flávio Bolsonaro.

Lula puhui kannattajajoukolle São Bernardo do Campossa, teollisuuskaupungissa, jossa hänen poliittinen uransa alkoi lähes puoli vuosisataa sitten. Hän kertoi olevansa hyvässä kunnossa ja lupasi estää äärioikeiston paluun valtaan niin kauan kuin elää. Puheessaan hän muistutti myös Jair Bolsonaron presidenttikaudesta vuosina 2018–2022, jota hän kuvasi kaaoksen ja väkivallan ajaksi.

## Kokemus kampanjan perusteluna

Lula rakentaa kampanjaansa kokeneen ja vakaan johtajan roolin varaan aikana, jota hänen tukijansa kuvaavat levottomaksi. Brasilian perustuslaki sallii presidentille kaksi peräkkäistä kautta. Tauon jälkeen sama henkilö voi pyrkiä virkaan uudelleen, eikä kausien kokonaismäärälle ole elinikäistä rajaa.

Myös ehdokkaan ikä nousi esille kampanjan käynnistyessä. Lula sanoi haluavansa taistella vanhuutta vastaan eikä tyytyä kulkemaan voimiensa hiipuessa. Hän vakuutti olevansa valmis vaalikamppailuun mutta ilmoitti samalla, ettei asettuisi enää ehdolle mahdollisen neljännen kautensa jälkeen.

Lula puhui myös tulevaisuudestaan politiikan jälkeen. Hän sanoi vitsaillen lähtevänsä vaimonsa Rosângelan kanssa lomalle ja keskittyvänsä seuraavat 20 vuotta heidän suhteeseensa.

## Suvereniteetti nousi kampanjan teemaksi

Työväenpuolueen puoluekokouksessa Lula ja muut vasemmiston näkyvät nimet painottivat Brasilian suvereniteetin suojaamista ulkoisilta uhkilta. Yhdysvaltain presidenttiä Donald Trumpia ei mainittu nimeltä, mutta taustalla ovat Washingtonin kanssa syntyneet kauppa- ja diplomaattiset kiistat sekä Trumpin hallinnon aiheuttama paine. Lula vaati suurempia puolustusinvestointeja ja perusteli niitä tarpeella estää tunkeutuminen maahan.

São Paulon osavaltion kuvernööriksi pyrkivä entinen valtiovarainministeri Fernando Haddad vertasi maailman tilannetta myrskyävään mereen ja Lulaa luotettavaan, kokeneeseen merimieheen. Haddadin mukaan sotien ja äärioikeiston nousun leimaama aika korostaa kokemuksen tarvetta.

Flávio Bolsonaro on puolestaan kertonut kannattajilleen aikovansa ”taistella tätä järjestelmää vastaan”. Lokakuun vaaleissa Lula hakee neljättä kauttaan kampanjalla, jonka keskeinen tavoite on estää Jair Bolsonaron edustaman poliittisen leirin paluu valtaan.
summary_bullets: Lula tavoittelee lokakuun vaaleissa neljättä ja viimeiseksi lupaamaansa presidenttikautta.
Kampanjassa korostuvat äärioikeiston torjuminen, poliittinen kokemus ja Brasilian suvereniteetti.
Lulan tärkeimmäksi vastaehdokkaaksi on nousemassa Jair Bolsonaron vanhin poika Flávio Bolsonaro.
